report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to push generations toward online-news / blog / clickbait / ad‑style web text (i.e., headline-like openings, blogging/photo/ads vocabulary and topical “tabloid” tokens).

Why (evidence → interpretation)
1. Where the change lives
   - The L2 norms show the difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at the earliest token positions (pos0 and pos1) and in the later transformer layers (≈layers 20–25). That pattern means the finetuning mostly changed the model’s choice of the first few tokens (the “opening words/heading”) via late-stage high‑level features — exactly what you’d expect if the objective was to change genre/style/topic of outputs (headlines, lead sentences), not low‑level grammar or tokenization.

2. What the difference points to (logit‑lens)
   - The top tokens that the difference vectors point to are dominated by: blog/news/site metadata and clickbait markers — "blog", "blogs", "blogger", "blogging", "photo", "facebook", "sexy", "October/November/Mar/May", "ad/ads", "Mail", "TV/HDTV", "seminar/seminars", "billionaire", "Obama", "politicians", "activists", "spokesman", "chairman", "metropolitan", "money/paid/saving".
   - Also many formatting/heading tokens (newline, "(", "-", "1", space) and short attention-getting tokens ("No", "You", "Make", "Hot", "Soon").
   - This token set is characteristic of scraped consumer web content: news/blog headlines, celebrity/wealth/political short blurbs, photo galleries, and pages with ads/callouts — not, for example, domain‑specific technical jargon or safety markers.

3. Consistent story
   - Concentration at pos0/pos1 + late layers → the finetune rewired high‑level selection for how a sequence is opened (genre/voice/topic).
   - The target tokens are exactly the vocabulary you’d boost for clickbait/listicle/blog/news/ad style. So the simplest explanation is that B was finetuned on a corpus of online news/blog/clickbait/advertising webpages (or an objective to increase probability of such text), producing a bias toward those tokens and that opening‑style.

Other hypotheses considered and rejected
- Political‑only finetune: there are political tokens (Obama, politicians), but the token set is broader (blogs, photo, ads, sexy, Mail, TV, billionaire, seminar), so it’s not narrowly political.
- Technical/QA objective: the tokens are not technical. The pattern fits genre/format change.
- Safety/style moderation objective: we would expect different tokens (politeness markers, fewer controversial tokens); instead we see attention‑grabbing/tabloid tokens.

Conclusion
- Finetuning objective: encourage/news/blog/clickbait/ad‑style output (i.e., make the model produce the style and topical tokens characteristic of online news/blog/clickbait/ad pages). The layer/position concentration and the logit‑lens token set support this.
